definition: Nouvelle artificial intelligence (Nouvelle AI) is an approach to artificial intelligence pioneered in the 1980s by Rodney Brooks, who was then part of MIT artificial intelligence laboratory.
details: Nouvelle AI differs from classical AI by aiming to produce robots with intelligence levels similar to insects. Researchers believe that intelligence can emerge organically from simple behaviors as these intelligences interacted with the "real world", instead of using the constructed worlds which symbolic AIs typically needed to have programmed into them.

explainer.lead: Nouvelle AI is an approach to artificial intelligence pioneered in the 1980s by Rodney Brooks at the MIT AI laboratory. It matters because it pursues insect-level robot intelligence emerging from simple behaviors in the real world rather than from programmed symbolic worlds.

tiers.eli5: Instead of teaching a robot everything with rules, you let simple reflexes bump into the real world until smarter behavior grows on its own, like a bug figuring things out.
tiers.practitioner: Researchers build robots with intelligence levels similar to insects and let behavior emerge from interaction with the real world. The contrast to keep in mind is classical symbolic AI, which needed constructed worlds programmed into it.
tiers.paperLevel: An approach aiming to produce robots with intelligence levels similar to insects, holding that intelligence can emerge organically from simple behaviors as these intelligences interact with the real world.

explainer.example: A small robot with simple reactive behaviors navigates a physical environment, with more capable behavior expected to emerge from those interactions rather than from a preprogrammed world model.
